sources.title: DoDM 5205.07 Volume 1 - DoD SAP Security Manual: General Procedures

claims.text: Purpose para 1.b.(1): the volume 'Assigns responsibilities, implements policy established in DoD Instruction (DoDI) 5205.11, and describes the general procedures for the administration of DoD SAP security,' and (2) 'Incorporates and cancels Revision 1 Department of Defense Overprint to the National Industrial Security Program (NISP) Operating Manual Supplement.' The 'NISPOM Supplement Overprint' -- the historic classified-annex mechanism for SAP industrial security -- was folded into this public manual in 2015.

claims.text: Enclosure 2, para 3 assigns the Director, DoD SAPCO -- 'Under the authority, direction, and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense' -- the roles of 'DoD designated proponent for developing and implementing policies and procedures for DoD SAP execution, management, and administration' and 'DoD single point of Congressional liaison concerning SAPs.'

claims.text: DoDM 5205.07-V1 Enclosure 2 para 2.c: 'Unless a carve-out provision is approved by the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense: (1) Performs SAP security inspections at cleared defense contractor locations ... (2) Authorizes classified contractor SAP information systems (ISs) and the introduction of guest systems in contractor SAP facilities (SAPFs). (3) Coordinates with the designated counterintelligence (CI) component to provide cross-sharing of threat and incident information affecting the security of the facility or its defense information or cleared personnel.'

claims.text: The FWAC rule is the structural reason an insider allegation about a SAP cannot travel through ordinary DoD hotline channels: the manual directs it back into the same compartment it concerns. Reasoning: SAP-channel-only reporting routes the complaint to officials inside the program.

desc: Volume 1 of the four-volume DoD SAP Security Manual assigns responsibilities and describes the general procedures for the administration of DoD SAP security, implementing the policy of DoDI 5205.11, and it incorporates and cancels the Revision 1 Department of Defense Overprint to the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual Supplement. Its Enclosure 2 contains the operative statement of what a carve-out removes. The Director, DSS - the office now called the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency - administers the NISP and issues facility clearances for defense contractors 'to include contractors performing on DoD SAPs'; but then, 'Unless a carve-out provision is approved by the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense', the Director performs SAP security inspections at cleared defense contractor locations, authorises classified contractor SAP information systems and the introduction of guest systems in contractor SAP facilities, and coordinates with the designated counterintelligence component to cross-share threat and incident information. Read the sentence backwards and it is an inventory of what disappears when a carve-out is signed: the independent physical inspection, the independent accreditation of the computers, and the independent counterintelligence feed. Its glossary supplies the definition in eleven words of substance: 'carve-out. A provision approved by the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense that relieves DSS of its NISP obligation to perform industrial security oversight functions for a DoD SAP.' Volume 1 also documents two cover mechanisms - HANDLE VIA SPECIAL ACCESS CHANNELS ONLY (HVSACO), an unclassified handling caveat used among other things 'When using a SAP nickname for an unacknowledged SAP', and the rule that 'Federal Government-affiliated identification cards will not be used for positive identification in unacknowledged locations'.
